correctness.rationale: Smooth projective bidegree (3,3) model gives canonical basis and genus 4. Exact Hasse differentiation computes W=(A^4−1)/A^8, and direct substitution of the osculating plane gives −A s^4(A s^2−s+A). This yields all 36 affine contacts, their residual divisor types and the explicit incidence components; boundary jets give six points of weight four and total Plücker degree 60. A standalone exact finite-field checker confirms the factorization for all A^4=1 and all finite graph components.

originality.rationale: The characteristic-three complete residual degree-two divisor for each of 36 order-four osculating planes and its 6 directed triangles/3 hexagons are not asserted in inspected primary sources. Korchmáros–Montanucci (2016-12) strongly covers underlying canonical local orders and therefore the special contact locus; it does not determine second residual intersections or the contact graph. The exact factorization and incidence classification require additional computations, beyond knowing contact order at P. Residual risk: unindexed calculations or straightforward unpublished consequences may predate this statement.
residual_risks: The 2016 preprint supplies strong contact-order data; specialized unpublished extensions could work out the residual quadratic identity.

value.rationale: The residual divisor of the unique fourth-order canonical osculating hyperplane is a natural intrinsic invariant, and the complete partition into six directed triangles of double residual contacts and three undirected hexagons of simple residual contacts reveals geometric structure not implied by point counts or local order sequences alone. It is a complete classification on a distinguished genus-four curve, with reproducible proof and arithmetic context.
